title: Graph-selected brain connectivity is associated with ADHD symptom scores
summary: A dynamic graph convolutional network analyzed resting-state scans from 603 ADHD-200 participants. Model-selected connectivity features were associated with symptom severity in a 172-person subgroup. These retrospective, post-selection associations are exploratory and do not establish a causal ADHD mechanism or clinical utility.
ai_technology: Dynamic graph convolutional network (dGCN) and isolation forest
organization: Lehigh University; University of Maryland; University of Pennsylvania; Georgia State University; Georgia Institute of Technology; Emory University

source_review.scope: Original publication metadata, computational Methods2.1/2.2.6, Results3.1/3.3.1–3.3.3 and limitations4.2 actually read; no author code executed.

evidence.tested: The selected four-site sample contained 260 ADHD and 343 control participants after isolation-forest outlier removal. dGCN combined connectivity with seven personal-characteristic variables and reached 72.0% diagnostic accuracy in site-stratified ten-fold cross-validation; leave-site-out accuracy ranged from 67.9% to 74.3%. Across 172 Peking University participants with symptom scales, regression on model-selected regional features yielded cross-validated symptom-score correlations of .33–.36. Selected within-frontal, within-posterior-fossa and subcortical–posterior-fossa connectivity showed symptom correlations of .28–.34, reported with FDR correction.
evidence.unknown: Regional selection used model weights averaged across diagnostic cross-validation. Its independence from the subsequent symptom regression and correlation analyses is not established; FDR correction does not remove selection bias. All symptom analyses used a subset of the same source dataset. Imaging alone did not supply the reported diagnostic predictions: age, sex, handedness and IQ-related inputs were included. Site-held-out classification is not independent replication of the selected biological associations. No causal direction, independent symptom-cohort confirmation or benefit from clinical use is established. The November2021 online version is represented; the issue date is February2022, and the bounded search does not establish earliest public priority.
evidence.ai_role: Learned graph convolutions ranked regional connectivity features used to investigate symptom associations; a separate conventional linear regression quantified symptom-score prediction. The claimed result is the exploratory AI-selected association, not a causal mechanism.
